label: Original-phase input of h/b/3/e/q at positions 2-6
explanation: Reset-gate unit that fires only during the original (input) phase, when the current input is one of a small token set: h (strongest, about 35% of mass), b, 3, e, q. It peaks at positions t=3-4 and is weak or silent at t=0-1 and t>=7. It never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase. Activation is graded by token: h > b > 3 > e > q. It fires on repeat occurrences of these tokens as well as first occurrences. Misses are low-magnitude firings on other tokens (g, z, v, 0) and hold about 7% of activation mass. False positives are mostly e/q at early positions where it stays below threshold. Dev F1 0.80, mass recall 0.93.

issues: Reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.794, R 0.810, F1 0.802, mass recall 0.934.

The profile backs the factual claims. The unit fires only in the original phase, never on the delimiter or in the copy phase. Activation mass by token is h 35%, b 25%, 3 17%, e 11%, q 6%. Activity peaks at t=3-4, is near zero at t=0-1, and is small at t>=7 (0.9% of mass).
The repeat-occurrence claim holds. Requiring no earlier h/b/3/e/q in the sequence drops F1 from 0.80 to 0.56. Restricting by to_go also lowers F1, so there is no hidden dependence on sequence end.
Misses on the test split (6.6% of activation mass) are scattered, low-magnitude firings on g, z, 0 and others, plus h/b at t=7. They do not form a systematic class.

Minor imprecision: false positives are not only e/q at early positions. h/b/3 sometimes stay below threshold too, mainly at t=2 and t=6. The best fix, per-token position windows (h/b/3 at t=2-7, e at t=2-6, q at t=3-5), raises test F1 by only about 0.016, to 0.818. That is a small refinement, not a refutation.
